entry.title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
entry.summary: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. We present, in an introductory way, the approach proposed in a recent series of works [Lett. Math. Phys. 114, 32 (2024): doi:10.1007/s11005-024-01777-0], [Rev. Math. Phys 38, 2461006 (2026): doi:10.1142/S0129055X24610063], [Commun. Math. Phys. 406, 201 (2025): 10.1007/s00220-025-05360-z] and [J. Math. Phys. 67, 022101 (2026): doi:10.1063/5.0311182] including a previously missing extension of the Gallavotti--Cohen (steady state) version of the FT to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting of quantum dynamical systems. We focus on the open quantum systems, where a small system interacts with several (infinitely extended) reservoirs, and discuss the following approaches: naive, two-time measurement, phase space contraction and ancilla state tomography. We review the connection with modular theory. The latter provides a way to extend the classical notions to the quantum domain. We discuss the quantum version of the principle of regular entropic fluctuations, introduced in the classical context in [Nonlinearity 24, 699 (2011): doi:10.1088/0951-7715/24/3/003]. Finally, we relate the statistical properties of these various notions of entropy production to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators and apply this approach to a paradigmatic model of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: the spin-fermion model. The results presented here shed a new light on the nature of entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics.

entry.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
entry.summary: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

entry.title: New Developments in Diagrammatic Monte Carlo for Interacting Lattice Fermions: Efficient Algorithms and Applications
entry.summary: This thesis develops diagrammatic methods for thermodynamic and subsystem quantities of interacting lattice fermions, providing reference calculations for quantum simulators and many-body approximations. I formulate an inverse-flavour expansion about a self-consistent Hartree saddle, enumerate non-Gaussian diagrams, and use a discrete Lehmann representation to integrate selected internal vertices analytically. Density results cover 31 state points of the six-flavour Hubbard model on a $70\times70$ lattice at $T/t=0.15$. I generalize combinatorial summation to flavour-dependent propagators and expansion shifts. CoS++ combines partial contractions to obtain connected sums for interaction subsets. A determinant-polynomial sieve evaluates the same sums through local coefficient filters; at ninth order it is 24--25 times faster than the specified CoS baselines in three-flavour dense-random-matrix benchmarks. Thermodynamic applications include a 2048-site honeycomb lattice and a three-flavour square lattice with 1024 sites. For the second Renyi entropy, I derive a fermionic replica path integral and a stable evaluation of its two-time Green functions. The connected-determinant calculation reaches tenth order on a $3\times3$ cluster and ninth order on larger lattices. On $50\times50$ sites at $(U/t,μ/t,βt)=(3,1,8)$, the ninth-order continuation at shift $α=1.3$ gives $S_2/N_s=0.06695$ with propagated Monte Carlo uncertainty $3.0\times10^{-5}$. Comparing two expansion shifts at their respective retained orders gives an endpoint difference of $2.6\times10^{-4}$.
entry.arxiv:comment: PhD thesis with extended derivations and additional technical details beyond those presented in the corresponding manuscripts

entry.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
entry.summary: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.

entry.title: Perturbation-Based Data Selection for Medical Question Answering
entry.summary: Selecting a compact training subset is an important step in adapting medical language models from existing question-answering banks. We investigate perturbation-based data selection using two signals derived from Gaussian perturbations of the final-block representation: prediction-change frequency and non-flipping margin contraction. After a shared entropy prefilter, Representation-Sensitivity Prioritization (RSP) combines the signals using automatic root-mean-square scaling, while RSP-Drop ranks candidates by contraction alone. Both selectors use only questions and answer options during selection. We evaluate them with MedGemma-4B on five medical QA datasets at retained-set budgets of 64, 128, and 256 examples. At the primary budget of 128, RSP and RSP-Drop obtain dataset-averaged Macro-F1 scores of 47.55 and 48.28, respectively, compared with 45.11 for entropy-pool-matched random selection. Their relative performance varies across datasets and budgets. A selected-set case study identifies contrasting clean-margin profiles among the examples exchanged by the two rules, while a full-pool ablation shows that entropy prefiltering is not uniformly beneficial. These retrospective results characterize the empirical utility and limitations of perturbation-based selection under a fixed adaptation protocol. Evaluation uses one backbone and benchmarks with documented training-family overlap; it does not establish clinical effectiveness.
entry.arxiv:comment: 10 pages. Preprint submitted to IEEE ICHI 2027. Extends the non-archival GenAI4Health @ NeurIPS 2026 study arXiv:2609.09684v2 with automatic RMS scaling, RSP-Drop, budget analyses, and entropy-prefilter ablations

entry.title: Entanglement entropy of evolving wormholes
entry.summary: We compute the entanglement entropy of a discretized scalar field in the fixed spacetime background of an evolving wormhole. Evolving wormholes are a class of time dependent and spherically symmetric wormhole geometries. In both expanding and contracting models, we find dynamically generated entanglement. Asymptotically far from the wormhole throat, the entanglement entropy is well described by the leading term in the area law, although its coefficient can depend sensitively on the value of the UV cutoff. As the UV cutoff is decreased, the coefficient becomes progressively less sensitive to the cutoff, providing numerical evidence that it approaches a cutoff-independent value in the continuum limit. Near the throat, we find a double-dip structure in the entanglement entropy which cannot be described by the leading and logarithmic contributions to the area law.

entry.title: Convergence Analysis of the Quantum Blahut-Arimoto Algorithm and the Contraction Coefficient of Qubit Amplitude-Damping Channels
entry.summary: In this work, we investigate the convergence rate of the quantum Blahut-Arimoto (BA) algorithm proposed for computing the coherent information of less noisy quantum channels. Previous work established exponential convergence under certain restrictive assumptions on the channel. Using a Taylor expansion around a positive definite optimizer, we show that, for an injective degradable channel whose degrading channel has a relative-entropy contraction coefficient strictly less than one, the algorithm converges at an exponential rate after sufficiently many iterations. We further verify this condition for qubit amplitude-damping (AD) channels in the relevant parameter regime. In addition, by analyzing the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric on the Bloch ball, we derive an explicit characterization of the relative-entropy contraction coefficient of qubit AD channels. The proposed approach is further extended to calculate the relative contraction coefficient and the relative expansion coefficient of two qubit AD channels.

entry.title: Thin-Shell Wormholes in Born--Infeld-Type Magnetic Spacetimes
entry.summary: We investigate the radial stability, thermodynamic balance, and bilateral disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes built from Born--Infeld-type magnetic exteriors. The exact lapse and junction conditions define a fixed-mass family in which magnetic self-energy ties the nonlinear scale to the charge. The shell has negative energy density, although an inner sampled region satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. Linear radial perturbations yield unstable calibrated barotropic samples and stable sectors for the generalized and modified cosmic Chaplygin laws on selected real branches. Analytic horizon and large-radius limits explain the stability transitions and show how the modified linear pressure term can replace outer stability with finite radial intervals. Minimally coupled Maxwell rays traverse transparent junctions between exteriors with a common arctangent emission profile, viewed by a static observer. The wormhole-black-hole intensity difference separates transmitted disk light from emission removed by throat excision. Compared with static emitters, circular and plunging motion reduce the face-on intensities in the studied cases; inclined motion generates strong azimuthal contrast. Increasing the subcritical charge contracts the critical circle and permits more disk crossings near it in the optical samples. Under a reversible first law, flux cancellation gives isentropic motion at positive temperature, with entropy dependence left to a constitutive completion. These results distinguish geometric, material, and kinematic effects on shell support and disk illumination.

entry.title: Rényi multi-entropy of graph states and the $n -> 1$ limit
entry.summary: Rényi multi-entropy extends the Rényi entropy to pure states of more than two parties. It is defined by a replica contraction at integer replica number $n$, and the multi-entropy is its $n\to1$ limit. In holography this limit is conjectured to compute the area of a minimal soap-film web in the bulk. Understanding multi-entropy for general states, however, is harder. Unlike the bipartite case, the replica contraction is not a moment of a density matrix, and the continuation to $n=1$ has to be found by other means. We study this problem for qubit graph states. We show that at every odd $n$ the contraction equals $2^{-k/2}$, where $k$ is a sum of ranks of matrices over a finite field, one row and one column per qubit. We define a class of graphs that we call collision-controlled, for which the rank sum is a polynomial in $n$. This class includes graphs without even cycles and all complete bipartite graphs. The natural polynomial $n \to 1$ continuation is a finite sum over partitions of the parties. While the Rényi multi-entropy is non-increasing under single-qubit Pauli measurements at every odd integer $n>1$, the continuation to $n=1$ is not. A $Z$ measurement on one qubit of an odd ring with $2r + 1 \geq 7$ qubits raises it from $(r+1)\log 2$ to $(2r-1) \log 2$. Thus the continuation is not an entanglement monotone.

entry.title: Rényi Multi-entropy for Stabilizer States: A Finite Field Gauss Sum Problem
entry.summary: Rényi multi-entropy probes multi-partite structure beyond bipartite spectra, but its behavior in general quantum states and the entanglement structure it captures remain poorly understood. We develop a finite field Gauss sum framework for calculating it in stabilizer states. Within this framework, the replica contraction reduces to a quadratic Gauss sum if and only if the state is locally unitarily equivalent to a stabilizer state. We obtain analytic expressions for the Rényi multi-entropy of all tree graph states and large families of loop graph states. In contrast to their flat bipartite Rényi spectra, stabilizer states generically have nonflat Rényi multi-entropy spectra.
entry.arxiv:comment: 42 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Lean 4 formalization sources: https://github.com/Alephice/stabilizer-renyi-multientropy-lean

entry.title: Energy Equality, Vectorial $L^1$ Contraction, and Mixed-Norm Stability for Parabolic Systems with Rough Skew-Symmetric Potentials
entry.summary: We consider Dirichlet parabolic systems with measurable, real skew-symmetric zero-order potentials on bounded Lipschitz domains in three dimensions. Although skew-symmetry formally removes the potential from the energy balance, singular coefficients may leave the product $CU$ merely integrable, so testing the equation with the solution is not justified. We overcome this obstruction through bounded-gradient entropy identities and stable approximation. For $C\in L^r(0,T;L^q(Ω;\mathbb R^{m\times m}))$ with $1\le r\le\infty$, $6/5\le q\le\infty$, and $2/r+3/q\le7/2$, we establish existence and uniqueness in the full energy--distributional class, exact energy equality at every pair of times, Euclidean-vector $L^1$ contraction, and strong convergence of both solutions and coefficient--solution products under strong coefficient approximation. We compare a vectorial entropy proof with a derivation by scalar entropies and spherical averaging, and explain the narrower roles of temporal regularization, convex invariance, and adjoint transposition. An application to diffusion--precession gives quantitative stability under $L^1$ perturbations of prescribed magnetic fields for bounded initial data, including singular fields outside the main mixed-norm range.

entry.title: Statistical Laws of Human Mobility under Large-Scale Behavioural Shock
entry.summary: Human mobility follows robust statistical laws, but whether these laws persist under large, sudden behavioural shocks remains unclear. Here we analyse privacy-enhanced GPS trajectories of over one million users in California and 180,000 in Massachusetts from January to September 2020, spanning the onset and easing of COVID-19 restrictions. During restrictions, individual ranges contracted below a characteristic scale of about 5 km, while short- and medium-range trip lengths and rare long-distance trips persisted. Exploration slowed from super-diffusive to near-diffusive, and visits concentrated on a few habitual locations. Trajectory shape, once rescaled, was preserved, and the entropy reduction is largely explained by fewer visited locations rather than more regular routines. Recovery after reopening was heterogeneous rather than a uniform return to baseline, and the decline began before mandatory orders. These results suggest that restrictions reorganised, rather than simply rescaled, individual mobility, with implications for mobility-based epidemic models.

entry.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. System-wise, exact residual supervision requires capturing, retaining, and reprocessing many trajectory-dependent states. ORL co-designs the algorithm with asynchronous residual capture and transport, specialized block-diffusion attention, and packed compute-balanced training, making it practical at scale. On a 4B DLM converted from Qwen3-4B, ORL improves tokens per forward (TPF) by up to 6.2x and, with our dlmrt engine, end-to-end throughput by approximately 6.9x at comparable or better quality. In single-request serving on one H100, this mode achieves a stronger speed-quality Pareto frontier than autoregressive models with EAGLE3 and DFlash speculative decoding under both strict and relaxed verification, running 1.74x faster than DFlash at matched accuracy. ORL also transfers to existing DLMs: on LLaDA-2.1-mini, 36 H100-hours and 4.2M self-generated tokens, about 10x less data than prior LLaDA recipes, yield up to 1.5x higher TPF and up to 3x higher throughput at comparable quality, and on DiffusionGemma, ORL raises TPF by 1.1-1.2x. With dlmrt and NVFP4 quantization, ORL models decode a single request at up to 5,046 tokens/s on one B200, 7,708 on eight B200s, and 2,788 on a consumer RTX 5090, with comparable quality.

entry.title: Routing Optimality for Demand Graphs of Matching Number at Most Two
entry.summary: We prove that network coding and fractional routing have the same capacity region in undirected networks whose demand graph has matching number at most two, that is, when no three demand edges have pairwise disjoint endpoints. The metric-packing reduction of Liu et al. reduces this problem to a distance-weighted communication inequality on the fixed graph $Γ_{3,3}$. We first prove two entropy inequalities for sessions between designated terminal pairs on $Γ_{3,3}$. We then extend this result to sessions with arbitrary endpoints to obtain the distance-weighted communication bound required by the reduction. The proof combines conditional entropy inequalities with two graph contractions and an information inequality for deterministic interaction. Combining this inequality with the existing reduction establishes routing optimality for this class of demand graphs.
entry.arxiv:comment: This paper has been submitted to ITW 2027

entry.title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning
entry.summary: We study stationary discrete-time mean-field games with finite state and action spaces under the average-reward criterion, with an entropy-regularized objective and population-dependent dynamics and rewards. Under a minorization condition, the soft Q-operator is a span-seminorm contraction for the full transition kernel, so relative value iteration does not require the minorizing measure. When the Lipschitz constant of the kernel is below the minorization mass and the temperature exceeds an explicit threshold, the equilibrium fixed-point operator is a contraction: an equilibrium exists, its population distribution is unique, and a fixed-point iteration converges to it geometrically. We then learn the equilibrium model-free from a simulator, combining soft Q-learning at a fixed population distribution with an empirical transition kernel. We prove a finite-sample bound for soft Q-learning in the span seminorm, with temperature-independent constants, and derive convergence rates for the learned population distribution and policy. A congestion-aware routing game illustrates the results.

entry.title: Uniqueness and stability of entropy waves among vanishing dissipation limits from the Navier--Stokes--Fourier System
entry.summary: In this paper, we establish the stability of general entropy wave solutions of the compressible Euler equations (that is, profiles with constant velocity and pressure) in the class of vanishing dissipation limits from the Navier--Stokes--Fourier system. If the initial data of our sequence of solutions to the Navier--Stokes--Fourier system converges to the initial data of the entropy wave solution, we further have convergence of the solutions to the entropy wave. This gives uniqueness and stability of the entropy wave in this class. The proof is based on the $a$-contraction theory.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Bounds for Fréchet Means of Dependent Data in Metric Spaces with Curvature Bounded Above
entry.summary: We prove finite-sample risk bounds for empirical quadratic and power Fréchet means in geodesic metric spaces with curvature bounded above for observations with arbitrary joint law. We compare the sample with exchangeable copies in which one observation is redrawn independently of the original sample and the others move to preserve the joint law. These displacements control the error, with no entropy or dimension assumptions. For quadratic Fréchet means, this yields a general ``coupling bound'' in any separable complete $CAT(κ)$ space, where for $κ>0$ the observations must lie in a closed convex set of circumradius below $π/(2\sqrtκ)$. This bound is exact on the real line for nonnegatively correlated Gaussian observations and for comonotone functions of a common factor. We apply it in two settings. Under local dependence, the resulting risk bound grows linearly with the average size of the dependency neighborhoods. Under transport sensitivity and for bounded metric variances, summable sensitivities of the conditional laws to a change in one observation preserve the parametric mean squared error rate, while nonsummable polynomial decay gives explicit slower rates. We verify transport sensitivity for stationary reversible Markov chains with Wasserstein-contractive kernels and for bi-Lipschitz images of Gaussian sequences. In the more challenging setting of heavy-tailed, dependent data with possibly infinite variance, we consider power Fréchet means of order $α\in(1,2)$. Under nonpositive curvature, we bound their $L^α$ risk assuming only finite $α$-th moments.

entry.title: Stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for a non-convex viscoelastic system
entry.summary: We investigate the time-asymptotic stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for non-convex viscoelastic system. By choosing delicate time-dependent shift functions to the viscous shock and suitable weight functions for the relative entropy, we succeed in proving the time-asymptotic stability of the composite of a viscous Liu shock and a rarefaction wave from two different characteristic families for the one-dimensional viscoelastic system with a cubic non-convex stress-strain relation by $a$-contraction method. Here the non-classical Liu shock can be either degenerate or non-degenerate, which can be seen as the system version of the scalar Oleinik shock. Note that both the shift and the weight functions are chosen quite differently in the two cases of nearly degenerate and fully non-degenerate. The paper represents the first time-asymptotic stability result for the composite waves consisting of both non-classical Liu shock and rarefaction wave from two different families for the non-convex physical system.

entry.title: Trainable Quantum-Native Language Models: Dissipative Memory, Capacity Limits, and Hardware Validation
entry.summary: We study byte-level autoregressive language models whose hidden state is a small quantum register, whose transitions are learned token-conditioned quantum channels, and whose next-byte probabilities come directly from Born-rule measurements without a learned classical vocabulary projection or softmax. In the fixed-width recurrent setting, unitary dynamics cannot contract or reset stored distinctions; experimentally, unitary recurrence loses to its retrained one-token control in every tested variant. Introducing learned dissipation, then token-conditioned dissipative gating, yields useful memory beyond one token. The gated model improves test negative log-likelihood by 0.20 +/- 0.03 nats/byte over retrained parameter-matched one-token controls at context length 12, and by 0.29-0.33 at longer contexts, but never beats retrained two-token controls. A key-value recall benchmark shows a width-dependent threshold: one stored pair meets the pre-registered accuracy bar at 4-5 memory qubits, two pairs at 6-7, and three pairs remain unsolved. This is consistent with, but does not establish, a capacity explanation for the short effective memory horizon. As a secondary result, one-qubit models reach lower stationary memory entropy than a heuristically optimized classical predictive frontier at matched error in 9/9 seeds. On IBM Heron hardware, computational-basis memory-register distributions show signal against a uniform null in 12/12 circuits across prefixes of up to 12 tokens, next-bit probabilities pass pre-registered accuracy bars at four-token prefixes, and bytes are generated autoregressively by sampling physically measured bit probabilities. The tested models are classically simulable and substantially worse than classical n-gram baselines. We claim no computational quantum advantage.

entry.title: Entanglement entropy and magic of ZX-diagrams
entry.summary: Entanglement and non-stabilizerness are complementary resources underlying the complexity of quantum states, yet extracting either quantity from large quantum circuits generally requires exponentially scaling resources. In diagrammatic approaches to quantum computation, such as the ZX-calculus, both quantities likewise typically require expensive tensor contractions that are not native to graphical rewriting. Here we show that both entanglement and magic can be efficiently estimated directly from ZX-diagrams. Flow enables efficient extraction of a normal form separating a potentially extensively entangled graph-state backbone from non-Clifford Pauli gadgets. This structure yields additive upper and lower bounds on bipartite entanglement entropy, which we further tighten through a preprocessing procedure that removes or merges redundant non-Clifford contributions. The same normal form gives an upper bound on logarithmic stabilizer extent. We benchmark these methods in random unitary and monitored circuits, and a circuit combining Trotterized Hamiltonian evolution with Clifford layers, finding that the resulting bounds remain informative even at large qubit numbers, circuit depths, and internal spider counts. Our results provide scalable probes of entanglement and non-stabilizerness of ZX-diagrams and establish a bridge between ZX-calculus and quantum many-body resource characterization, with applications across quantum computing, quantum information, and condensed-matter physics.

entry.title: Intermediate coverings, random images, and projections
entry.summary: We study intermediate coverings of spectral families, Cantor sets, and projections of measures. Two perturbation families of a fixed ReLU tangent kernel have identical source thresholds. Their Brownian images have equal box thresholds and distinct intermediate thresholds, almost surely along prescribed geometric scales. For Cantor sets with delayed contractions, we obtain entropy formulas for the intermediate dimensions of the sets and their fractional Brownian images. These formulas yield endpoint asymptotics and a sharp separation theorem for the first phase transition. An oscillating variant has distinct lower and upper intermediate dimensions while preserving the Assouad spectrum. Finally, almost every orthogonal projection preserves both intermediate dimensions of a nonzero finite compactly supported measure whose quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension.

entry.title: Beyond Nominal Equilibria: Risk-Averse Multi-Population Mean-Field Games
entry.summary: Recent advances in mean-field games and its multi-population variants enable large-scale heterogeneous multi-agent systems to be modeled through representative agents and their associated mean-field distributions. However, existing approaches do not explicitly account for uncertainty in the behavior of other populations. To this end, we introduce a new paradigm: risk-averse multi-population mean-field games, where each population optimizes a worst-case expected reward over dynamically feasible ambiguity sets of mean-field flows of a subset of the other populations. Employing an occupation-measure formulation along with tools from set-valued analysis, we establish, under mild assumptions, several theoretical properties of the multi-population game, including the geometric properties of the ambiguity sets and the existence of a novel risk-averse multi-population mean-field equilibrium. Further, we derive contractivity results of the fixed-point operator under entropy regularization and show that it can be utilized to learn the equilibrium. Finally, we propose a risk-averse fictitious-play scheme and show that exploitability decays to zero, despite the additional nonlinearity introduced by the worst-case objective. We report several numerical experiments to illustrate convergence and risk-averse behavior.
entry.arxiv:comment: Submitted to a conference; comments are welcome

entry.title: Symmetric Grassmann Formulas: Monotone Dimension-Defect Hierarchies
entry.summary: We study the dimension defect of finitely many subspaces over an arbitrary field. We derive a symmetric, nonrecursive Grassmann-type formula for the dimension of their sum. The formula expresses the total dimension loss through intersections of a distinguished subspace with partial sums of the remaining subspaces, with coefficients determined by the number of subspaces involved. We also show that the formula admits a Shapley-value interpretation for the associated representable polymatroid. Grouping the correction terms by the number of participating subspaces yields a nonnegative dimension-defect profile. We prove that this profile is monotone and identify its successive gaps with the discrete curvatures of the average-rank profile. These gaps give exact remainders in two-sided defect bounds. Equality in either bound holds precisely when the images of the subspaces in the quotient by their common intersection form an internal direct sum. We also give an exact geometric decomposition of the Kinser slack into nonnegative quotient dimensions and characterize equality. Averaging these slacks over permutations and contractions recovers every defect curvature except the final one; additional representability constraints remain in the individual ordered slacks. Weighted and dual formulas accompany the expansion, and entropy analogues express the defect levels and curvatures as averages of mutual and conditional mutual information, respectively.

entry.title: A constrained Wasserstein gradient flow for mean-field Langevin dynamics
entry.summary: In the continuity of [1, 2, 3], we study a class of constrained mean-field Langevin dynamics formulated as a Wasserstein gradient flow with an energy constraint. We show that the constrained evolution therefore defines a well-posed dissipative dynamics in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$. We prove that the flow preserves probability mass and the energy constraint, dissipates the free energy monotonically, and converges exponentially to a unique constrained equilibrium under geodesic convexity assumptions. Using synchronous coupling, under Lipschitz assumptions, we demonstrate the quantitative $L^2$-propagation of chaos with a Fournier-Guillin bound, and under conditions of sufficient dissipativity, we derive an explicit time-uniform bound. We also demonstrate exponential controls in the $\mathcal{W}_2$ Wasserstein metric and the contraction of the invariant measure map. Using log-Sobolev inequalities, we show that the mean-field entropies decay exponentially along the constrained flow. The results are applied to several concrete and original examples. Keywords and phrases: Wasserstein gradient flows $\bullet$ mean-field Langevin dynamics $\bullet$ constrained nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations $\bullet$ Lagrange multiplier $\bullet$ JKO scheme $\bullet$ propagation of chaos $\bullet$ synchronous coupling $\bullet$ exponential ergodicity $\bullet$ functional inequality $\bullet$ log-Sobolev inequality $\bullet$ transport inequality $\bullet$ Talagrand T 2 -inequality

entry.title: Entropy Contraction and Hypercontractivity for Gaussian Quantum Markov Semigroups
entry.summary: In this paper, we study finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant Gaussian state. We present an algebraic characterization of the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality relative to the fixed-point algebra, and we obtain the corresponding optimal constant under the assumption that the drift evolution $e^{t\mathbf{Z}}$ converges as $t\to\infty$. We establish hypercontractivity for such quantum Markov semigroups with Hurwitz drift, in the sense that every fixed pair $1<p<q<\infty$ is attained at sufficiently large times. We find that the usual reverse hypercontractive curves with a positive rate from time zero can fail in general, but every fixed pair $1/2 < p < q < 1$ is attained at sufficiently large times under the Hurwitz assumption. We also systematically investigate the $p$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality and show that the $p$-logarithmic Sobolev constant can be negative for $0 < p < 1/2$.

entry.title: A Dichotomy for Planar Graph Homomorphisms with Nonnegative Weights
entry.summary: We prove a complete complexity dichotomy for planar graph homomorphism counting with any fixed symmetric nonnegative matrix of arbitrary finite order, giving an explicit criterion for tractability. We also characterize exactly which fixed positive vertex weights preserve tractability, with both classifications extending from algebraic weights to fixed real weights in a prescribed exact representation. Our proof hinges on an entropy-based continuation argument: maximal logarithmic support identifies distance kernels as maximum-entropy completions, extending their positive definiteness throughout the parameter interval. This enables distance geometry to recover hidden product coordinates even when planar gadgets cannot distinguish colors; counting-hardness arguments then force the factors to be zero-field Boolean Ising interactions. The classification also yields complete tractability criteria for clock models, coupled Ising systems, and planar contractions of stoquastic imaginary-time kernels. All results have been formally verified in Lean 4.

entry.title: CurveCodec 2: Skeleton-agnostic animation compression with a learned entropy model
entry.summary: Skeletal motion is stored as every joint's transform at every frame, yet most of it is implied by the body rather than by what the motion is about. Compression is one way to ask what a motion must still say once the body is known, and a production codec must answer it for any skeleton with a stated error bound. Our earlier codec, CurveCodec, matched the mean error of ACL, the production library of modern game engines, with a learned prior over sparse anchors, but not ACL's worst case, and it counted its payload as floats rather than bits. Here we ask where the redundancy of skeletal motion lies and which part of a codec a learned model should take over. Measurements give three answers. At production precision the largest saving comes from predicting each quantized curve from its own past, the second from choosing per joint, in closed loop through the hierarchy, which samples not to code. On the gaps such an encoder leaves, a nearest-neighbour oracle over millions of training samples is no better than linear interpolation, and no learned in-betweener we tried paid for itself. What a network does learn is the distribution of the residuals the codec must send. CurveCodec 2 codes every sub-track as a curve in the log map, quantized in closed loop and thinned to rate-distortion-selected keys, with residuals entropy-coded under a small learned model whose integer inference is bit-exact across platforms. Two contracts are verified on every decoded clip: ACL's own worst case per joint within a stated tolerance, or ACL's mean error per clip. On a held-out test side of 4,472 clips from 33 datasets, CurveCodec 2 needs 0.37x ACL's bytes at ACL's default precision of 0.01 cm under the worst-case contract and 0.22x at 0.1 cm under the mean contract, decodes on one CPU core, and transfers without retraining to a species absent from training. Project page: https://rubbly.cn/publications/curvecodec/

entry.title: Weak-BV stability of inflow and outflow problems for the isentropic Euler system
entry.summary: We study the well-posedness of small BV solutions to the one-dimensional isentropic Euler system on the half-line under inflow and outflow boundary conditions. These boundary conditions are formulated in terms of admissible trace sets determined by Navier--Stokes boundary layers and zero-speed shocks. For both the inflow and outflow problems, we construct small BV solutions taking values in the subsonic region. These solutions are unique and satisfy the quantitative stability estimate \begin{align*} \|U(\cdot, t)-V(\cdot, t)\|_{L^2} \lesssim \sqrt{\|U(\cdot, 0) - V(\cdot, 0)\|_{L^2}} \, , \end{align*} which holds for any such small BV solution $V$ and any $L^\infty$ entropy solution $U$ satisfying the strong trace property and the inflow/outflow boundary conditions. In particular, we emphasize that $U$ may take values outside the subsonic region and need not have bounded variation or be constructed by the front tracking scheme. This establishes the first weak-BV stability and uniqueness theory for inflow and outflow initial-boundary value problems. A key difficulty lies in verifying that the boundary set is compatible with the $a$-contraction framework, and in proving that the front-tracking limit satisfies the prescribed inflow/outflow conditions.

entry.title: In CEM, a World Model Is Also a Proposal Mechanism
entry.summary: The cross-entropy method (CEM) uses world-model scores to select action sequences and fit the distribution sampled in its next iteration. A scoring error can therefore change both the present decision and the candidates considered later. We evaluate these two roles separately. Four types of predictive model generate CEM traces, and every model rescores every saved candidate pool. Executing the same candidates in the environment provides a reference elite set and proposal update. Across twelve independently trained task-seed units on Walker and Cheetah, the pre-specified proposal distance falls from the first to the final CEM iteration in every unit. Proposal widths contract and fitted means separate relative to the remaining search width. Pairwise ranking agreement stays near chance on Walker and declines on Cheetah; elite-set agreement does not improve. This comparison shows greater variation between scorers than between pool sources on Cheetah; Walker has variation in both and in their pairings. We use the original six units to select Random nonlinear for a one-update intervention, without inspecting intervention outcomes. Replacing its first model-ranked update with an environment-ranked update lowers final realised selected-sequence cost in those six units and in six further units held out from the selection.

entry.title: Weighted Power Fréchet Means in Metric Spaces with Curvature Bounded Above
entry.summary: We establish non-asymptotic risk bounds for power Fréchet means in geodesic metric spaces with curvature bounded above. The observations form weighted, possibly infinite sequences of independent random variables whose laws and means may differ. We treat three settings. For $2$-Fréchet means in Hadamard spaces, we obtain a sharp mean squared error bound that becomes an identity in Hilbert spaces. For $2$-Fréchet means in CAT($κ$) spaces with $κ>0$, we establish variance and Wasserstein contraction inequalities with optimal constants depending on the circumradius $\varrho$ of the closed convex data domain, and obtain mean squared error bounds throughout the maximal range $\varrho<π/(2\sqrtκ)$. For $α$-Fréchet means in Hadamard spaces, $1<α<2$, we derive finite $L^α$ risk bounds under weighted $α$-moment conditions, allowing even an infinite $α$-moment of the population mixture. The proofs combine variance, quadruple, and contraction inequalities with a leave-one-out stability technique. Applications give prior and posterior bounds for Dirichlet-process Fréchet means and finite-sample guarantees for local constant Fréchet regression. The regression results require no response-space entropy condition and replace density smoothness assumptions common in earlier work with transport smoothness; for $α<2$, the bounds remain finite even when the responses have infinite variance.

entry.title: Shock profiles for the Navier--Stokes--Fourier--Poisson system under the Boltzmann relation
entry.summary: The one-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier--Poisson system under the Boltzmann relation is studied for the existence of small-amplitude viscous shock profiles connecting the Rankine--Hugoniot states of the quasineutral Euler system with effective pressure $P_{\mathrm{eff}}=ρ(θ+1)$. This profile is unique up to translation, of Lax type, and orbitally stable in time without a zero-mass assumption on the perturbation. The proof is based on a center-manifold reduction of the traveling-wave ODE and on the method of $a$-contraction with shifts, together with a relative-entropy functional augmented by electric energy and a sharp estimate of the viscous flux associated with $P_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

entry.title: Signatures of Bulk Topology from the 't Hooft Worldsheet
entry.summary: We study entanglement entropy in a certain ansatz of matrix quantum mechanics (MQM) wavefunctions which behave as generating functionals for a planar 't Hooft expansion. We argue that these 't Hooft diagrammatics can directly probe aspects of the topology of the bulk dual, such as the contractibility of a thermal or replica $S^1$ cycle. Our argument relies on treating 't Hooft diagrams as a non-perturbative definition of off-shell string theory worldsheets in which contractibility of replica cycle leads to worldsheets punctured by a conical deficit (as first described by Susskind and Uglum). We describe how a deconfinement transition in the MQM is tied to the exchange of dominant topologies, as well as to a candidate description of open string 'edge modes' of Susskind and Uglum. Lastly, we study toy models of black hole evaporation and show that the boundary planar expansion itself diagnoses the exchange of dominance between the disconnected topology and replica wormhole topology, without ensemble averaging and without independently postulating which bulk saddles should be included.

entry.title: Braid Stability and a Floer theory of Braid Isotopies
entry.summary: We build a Floer theory on the space of braids of periodic orbits of a Hamiltonian flow on a closed symplectic surface. The differential and continuation maps are defined by counting Floer isotopies of braids: tuples of Floer cylinders with pairwise disjoint graphs. With this new perspective, we prove a quantitative braid stability result that shows the persistence of braids under possibly large Hamiltonian perturbations. As an application, we show that for every $α\geq 0$ there is a sequence of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms $φ_k$ on the two-torus $T^2$ such that $$d_H(\operatorname{Ent}_{\leq α}(T^2,ω),φ_k)\to \infty \quad (k \to \infty),$$ where $\text{Ent}_{\leq α}(T^2,ω)\subset \text{Ham}(T^2,ω)$ denotes the set of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with topological entropy at most $α$ and $d_H$ the Hofer metric. We prove this result by studying only contractible periodic orbits, whereas analogous higher-genus statements were previously obtained using non-contractible orbits.

entry.title: Gravity, Entropy, and the Second Law: A Pedagogical Perspective
entry.summary: An interesting question for discussion in university physics courses is whether gravity can conflict with the second law of thermodynamics. In this work, we address this question by comparing the behavior of an ideal gas in two conceptually different regimes: one in which gravitational effects can be neglected and another in which self-gravity becomes important. In the first case, free expansion provides the familiar example in which an increase in the volume accessible to the gas leads to an increase in entropy. Self-gravitating systems behave differently: gravitational contraction can reduce the volume occupied by matter while releasing energy and increasing the entropy of the surroundings. This illustrates why the usual intuition that increasing entropy necessarily corresponds to increasing spatial dispersion cannot be applied directly to self-gravitating systems. Using elementary thermodynamic arguments and a minimal amount of mathematics, we discuss this apparent tension and show how entropy must be considered for the complete system, including emitted radiation. The discussion is finally extended to black holes and Hawking radiation, where the appropriate framework is the generalized second law of thermodynamics. The analysis is intended to provide a pedagogical bridge between elementary thermodynamics and some of the distinctive thermodynamic properties of gravitating systems.

entry.title: Verifiable Randomness for Blockchain-Based Lottery Systems
entry.summary: As lotteries and other high-stakes decentralized applications increasingly depend on unpredictable randomness for their operations, the lack of a secure and transparent on-chain random number generator that is verifiable by all participants remains a critical open problem. Various approaches to blockchain-based random number generation have emerged over the years, each with their own strengths and limitations, and have consistently been superseded as blockchain technology evolved. This paper surveys existing approaches to on-chain randomness and proposes a new platform that builds upon the well-known commit-and-reveal scheme while directly addressing its principal vulnerability, the last revealer attack, in which the final participant can withhold their reveal in order to bias or abort the output upon seeing an unfavorable result. We further compare this solution with prior approaches and evaluate its entropy properties. The proposed architecture combines a web-based front-end with a Solidity smart contract deployed on the Polygon 2.0 blockchain. Implemented and tested on the Amoy testnet, the prototype is low-cost and simple to deploy, providing a practical, accessible proof-of-concept for verifiable on-chain randomness.
